spec_match.rationale: Covers the direction-sensitivity angle properly: LTR right-edge vs RTL left-edge ellipsis across Arabic, Hebrew and Persian samples plus full-width LTR/RTL URL bars, which is exactly the writing-direction claim the feature makes.

interactive.rationale: Six focusable fields with live badges, a width slider and font-size toggle that re-style the inputs, and two full-width URL bars — a genuine tester, not a code-card (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card's promise (six fields, three RTL scripts, width slider, font toggle, full-width URL bars) matches the page one-for-one.

edge_cases.rationale: RTL scripts and width/font permutations are real edge coverage, but genuinely bidirectional content (mixed LTR URL inside RTL text is present only as a static value), vertical writing modes, and non-input ellipsis contexts are not explored.

conformance.rationale: The shared feature suite runs 9 pass / 0 fail here, but it checks prerequisites only and has no direction-aware or focused-state assertion, so it cannot fail on a pre-149 browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): all six cards render with correct-direction ellipsis, RTL inputs right-aligned, conformance panel 9/0/0; focus transitions, the slider and the font toggle were not driven. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

telemetry_health.rationale: Only the server-injected baseline telemetry is present; no custom interaction/assert events for the direction tests.

design_system.rationale: Nearly all colours are variables and .toggle-btn.active sets background and color together, but .test-input:focus uses raw `background: white` instead of a design-system variable.

accessibility.rationale: The six dynamically built inputs have no accessible name at all (card titles are unassociated), the font-size toggle buttons lack aria-pressed, .test-input removes outline relying only on a border-colour change, and badges are not live regions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The grid collapses to one column at 600px and wide inputs are width:100% box-sizing:border-box, rendering clean at 1280px headless; the ≈360px touch class and the 260px slider extreme were not exercised.

openQuestions.title: Name the six generated inputs accessibly
openQuestions.detail: buildGrid() creates <input> elements with no label, aria-label or association to the .card-title above them, so a screen reader announces six anonymous edit fields — on a page whose index card carries an 'Accessibility' tag. Attach the card title via <label> or aria-label (e.g. 'RTL — Hebrew long sentence test field'), add aria-pressed to the Normal/Large toggle, and restore a visible focus indicator that does not rely solely on border-colour.

openQuestions.title: Replace the hard-coded 'clipped at …' focus readout with an honest label or a measurement
openQuestions.detail: On focus the overflow-viz always prints 'clipped at left/right' regardless of whether the browser actually switches to clip — the probe cannot return false. Either measure an observable (compare input scrollWidth/scrollLeft reachability before/after focus) or label it 'Chrome 149+ clips here — manual observation'.

openQuestions.title: Use a design-system variable for the focused input background
openQuestions.detail: .test-input:focus sets background: white, bypassing the ivory/paper palette (invariant 5). Use var(--bg-ivory) or var(--bg-paper).

openQuestions.title: Add a true bidi edge case
openQuestions.detail: The page title promises bidirectional text, but every field is single-direction; the only mixed content (a URL embedded in RTL) appears in the static RTL URL bar. Add a field mixing Latin and Arabic runs where the ellipsis side and caret traversal order are genuinely surprising, which is the hardest case for this fix.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot and DOM dump of /v149/clip-text-overflow-on-user-interaction/overflow-direction-tester/ plus the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 9 pass / 0 fail / 0 blocked). Rendering is correct — LTR fields ellipsise at the right edge, Arabic/Hebrew/Persian fields at the left, URL bars show direction-appropriate truncation — but focus transitions, the width slider and font toggle were not driven headless. The substantive gap is accessibility: the generated inputs are nameless, which fails the page's own 'Accessibility' tag.
